title: Continuatio Fragmentorum ex Adversariis mathematicis depromptorum

errors: Printed p in the first part is (7ζζ−2ζη+ηη)/5. The correct value from p = (αβ+εζ)/2, or from p = s+εζ, is (2ζζ−2ζη+ηη)/5. This is confirmed three ways: Euler's own p²+s² factorisation is right only with 2ζζ; q²+r² contains the factor 5p = 2ζζ−2ζη+ηη; and the general solution with f = g = 1, h = −1 gives p = 2ζζ−2ζη+ηη. The '7' is a misprint (or a slip by the copyist or editor).
The transcription reads '−ε = γ−β', but the computation (ε = (3ζ−η)/5) requires ε = γ−β, consistent with α/ε = (η−ζ)/(γ−β). The stray sign is a transcription or print artefact.

The 'Solutio generalior' does not actually generalise: after imposing the divisibility condition gh = −f², it reduces to the special solution under ζ→fζ, η→gη. Euler himself notes this on the next page, so this is not an error, just a null result.

The general quotient printed as ff ηη + (3ffh/g + 4hh) ζζ is correct only under the first condition f²+gh = 0 (where it equals ff ηη + hh ζζ). It is a conditional rather than a general quotient, but harmless.

ideas.what: Parametrising four quantities by multiplicative factorisation of p±s, q±r with shared factors (α, β, γ, ε, ζ, η), exploiting homogeneity so that only ratios matter
ideas.modern_name: Rational parametrisation of a quadric intersection via factorisation of sums and differences; projective (homogeneous) parameters
ideas.where_published: Used throughout Euler's Diophantine papers and Vollständige Anleitung zur Algebra II; exact source of this fragment is the Adversaria (A. m. T. I p. 17-21)

ideas.what: Requiring one binary quartic (q²+r²) to be divisible by a binary quadratic (p) to cancel factors in a square condition; the conditions factor as (f²+gh)(4gh−3f²) = 0
ideas.modern_name: Common-factor / resultant condition for binary forms

ideas.what: Reduction of the problem to λ·(quadratic)·(two linear forms) = square
ideas.modern_name: Quartic (genus-1) curve, i.e. a quadratic twist of an elliptic curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler's square-condition methods; the elliptic-curve interpretation is modern (Poincaré onwards)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine Diophantine parametrisation from the Adversaria. The generalisation collapses back to the known special solution, which Euler recognises himself. The only noteworthy item is a misprint in p (7ζζ for 2ζζ). The underlying problem is not identified on this page, and the final quartic square condition is left untouched, but this is a standard, not a hidden, open end.
transcription_corrections: '−ε = γ − β' should read 'ε = γ − β' (as the subsequent ε = (3ζ−η)/5 requires).
p = (7ζζ − 2ζη + ηη)/5 as printed is mathematically wrong; the correct value is (2ζζ − 2ζη + ηη)/5 (a print error, not merely an OCR one, if the image indeed shows 7).
'unde fit p = (ff − gh)ζζ − 2fgζη + ggηη, s = g(hζζ − fζη + gηη)'; the OCR noise in this line should be ignored. The formulas are as given and verified.
